# RFC-0001: Disposable agent Kubernetes cliques

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @tlrmchlsmth

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0001:C-SUMMARY] System summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-summary"></a>

Oubliette will create disposable vCluster-backed Kubernetes environments for agent-spawned LLM-serving cliques. Agents receive broad authority inside their virtual control plane while independent host admission, resource, network, and lifecycle controls bound the real workloads.

---

## 2. Specification

---

## 3. Scope

### [RFC-0001:C-PURPOSE] Purpose and scope (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-purpose"></a>

Oubliette MUST provision short-lived, agent-scoped Kubernetes control planes whose workloads execute on an operator-controlled host cluster. Each clique MUST have an independently administered virtual API and a dedicated host enforcement boundary.

### [RFC-0001:C-NON-GOALS] Initial non-goals (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-non-goals"></a>

Multi-node prefill/decode, WideEP, host Kueue gang scheduling, LWS, JobSet, Gateway API, EPP, and a production DRA path are not required for the first milestone. They remain later decisions or validation tracks.

---

## 4. Security

### [RFC-0001:C-API-ISOLATION] Host API isolation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-api-isolation"></a>

An agent MUST authenticate only to its virtual Kubernetes API and MUST NOT receive credentials that authenticate to the host API. Virtual cluster-admin authority MUST NOT grant visibility or mutation of host cluster-scoped resources. Host synchronization MUST be explicitly allowlisted.

### [RFC-0001:C-HOST-ENFORCEMENT] Host-enforced workload policy (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-host-enforcement"></a>

Every synchronized workload MUST pass host-side admission that the virtual administrator cannot modify or bypass. Host policy MUST reject privileged containers, hostPID, hostIPC, hostNetwork, hostPath, and unapproved capabilities or runtime classes. Any inference exception, including IPC_LOCK, hugepages, or bounded shared memory, MUST be explicit and narrower than the general workload policy.

### [RFC-0001:C-NETWORK-ISOLATION] Clique network isolation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-network-isolation"></a>

Host pod networking MUST default deny traffic outside the clique, permit required intra-clique traffic, and restrict egress to an operator allowlist. RDMA access MUST come from an operator-owned profile that declares its enforced isolation scope and trust domain. Mutually untrusted cliques MUST NOT share an RDMA trust domain; they require per-clique isolation, exclusive placement, or a stricter operator boundary. Transport evidence MUST NOT be presented as proof of a stronger fabric isolation scope.

### [RFC-0001:C-AGENT-RUNTIME] Consumer-owned agent sandbox (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-agent-runtime"></a>

Every model-driven agent process MUST execute inside an approved sandbox owned by its consumer. Oubliette MUST NOT depend on one sandbox implementation, and host safety MUST remain valid if the consumer sandbox is compromised. OpenShell is the first-class resident and bootstrap integration; consumers such as Crucible MAY provide their own sandbox. Neither resident nor external agents may receive host Kubernetes credentials.

---

## 5. Lifecycle

### [RFC-0001:C-LIFECYCLE] Bounded lifecycle and cleanup (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-lifecycle"></a>

Host quota, admission, and network controls MUST exist before an agent receives a virtual kubeconfig. TTL expiry, explicit removal, or agent completion MUST trigger idempotent teardown of the virtual control plane, dedicated host namespace, synchronized objects, credentials, and storage. Cleanup completion MUST be externally observable even when the agent does not cooperate.

---

## 6. Scheduling

### [RFC-0001:C-RESOURCE-BOUNDS] Resource accounting (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-resource-bounds"></a>

Every clique MUST use an operator-owned resource profile that bounds pod count, GPU and device allocation, RDMA access, hugepages, storage, and service exposure on the host. Agent input MUST NOT contain raw host resource names, namespace names, synchronization rules, isolation scopes, trust domains, or policy exceptions.

---

## 7. Observability

### [RFC-0001:C-OBSERVABILITY] Scoped observability and provenance (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-observability"></a>

Host telemetry MUST attribute GPU and workload metrics to a clique without exposing other tenants. Benchmark evidence MUST record immutable inputs, component versions, exact measurement windows, virtual and host object lineage, transport proof, admission results, and teardown inventory.

---

## 8. Milestones

### [RFC-0001:C-MILESTONE-ZERO] Bootstrap milestone acceptance (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-milestone-zero"></a>

Milestone 0 MUST allow an agent in an approved consumer-owned sandbox to create a stub-tier Oubliette through the authenticated MCP lifecycle interface. The consumer integration MUST deliver virtual-cluster access outside the MCP transcript. Using that access, the agent MUST be able to create and observe an arbitrary namespaced workload through the virtual Kubernetes API. Explicit deletion and TTL expiry MUST remove the virtual control plane, derived host namespace, synchronized objects, credentials, and storage without agent cleanup. Milestone 0 does not require GPUs, RDMA, Kueue, or production observability.

### [RFC-0001:C-MILESTONE-ONE] First milestone acceptance (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-milestone-one"></a>

The first milestone MUST run two synchronized inference pods on one GPU node, account for each pod's RDMA access through a bounded operator-provided resource request, record its declared isolation scope and trust domain, and enforce host admission and default-deny pod networking. Evidence MUST prove KV traffic traverses the intended RDMA backend and device rather than pod networking, shared memory, CUDA IPC, TCP, or another fallback. TTL teardown MUST remove all Oubliette-owned host artifacts without agent cleanup.

---

## 9. Interfaces

### [RFC-0001:C-AGENT-INTERFACE] Agent lifecycle interface (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-agent-interface"></a>

Agents MUST manage Oubliette lifecycle through an authenticated MCP interface whose initial operations are create, get, list, renew, and delete. After readiness, agents MUST use the virtual Kubernetes API directly for in-Oubliette operations. The MCP interface MUST NOT proxy the host Kubernetes API, expose host credentials, accept raw host policy controls, or return kubeconfig material in tool results. Consumer integrations MUST deliver virtual-cluster access outside model transcripts.
